prompt: Two implementations of reserve share a signature. One buffers a reservation; the other commits it immediately. The caller expects to reserve two items atomically. What is the main issue?

options.text: The return type must be different for each implementation.
options.explanation: The problem is when saving happens, not the ID type. An immediate commit can leave the first item saved if the second fails.

options.text: The implementations disagree about transaction behavior in the contract.
options.explanation: The caller needs both reservations to succeed or fail together. An implementation that commits its own item breaks that expectation.

options.text: An interface call always buffers data, so the second implementation cannot commit.
options.explanation: Calling through an ABAP interface does not itself control commits. Each implementation must follow the agreed save rules.

options.text: The problem is resolved by returning a reservation ID earlier.
options.explanation: Returning the ID sooner does not undo an early commit. The implementation must preserve the required save behavior.

prompt: A quote interface accepts every positive quantity. A new implementation rejects quantity 1 and accepts only 10 or more. What best describes the change?

options.text: Compatible, because both methods have identical parameter types.
options.explanation: The types match, but valid inputs have changed. Existing callers are still entitled to ask for one unit.

options.text: Compatible, because callers can inspect the concrete class first.
options.explanation: Callers should not have to inspect concrete classes to use the promised interface. This would move the broken promise into every caller.

options.text: Incompatible with the stated contract because it narrows valid inputs.
options.explanation: The new provider rejects quantities that the shared rules explicitly allow. It cannot safely replace the existing provider for those callers.

options.text: Incompatible only if the implementation uses inheritance.
options.explanation: The same obligation applies to a class implementing the interface directly. Inheritance is not required for this compatibility problem.

prompt: An exporter and notifier share cancel behavior, have unrelated lifecycles, and one already inherits a framework class. What is the strongest starting design?

options.text: A narrow cancellation interface with shared policy composed as needed.
options.explanation: A small cancellation interface describes the shared operation. Each service can use a validation helper without joining an unrelated class hierarchy.

options.text: A common abstract superclass primarily to reuse a validation helper.
options.explanation: The services do not share a suitable base process here. A common superclass also conflicts with the existing framework superclass.

options.text: A concrete-class switch in each caller invoking unrelated methods.
options.explanation: Every caller would need to know the concrete classes. A common cancellation interface keeps that implementation knowledge out of callers.

options.text: A single static class that stores both objects' mutable state.
options.explanation: Combining unrelated mutable data creates new lifetime and state problems. It does not give callers a clear shared cancellation operation.

prompt: A subclass redefines an inherited format method but wants an additional mandatory parameter. Which approach respects ABAP method rules?

options.text: Add the parameter in REDEFINITION; base callers receive an initial value.
options.explanation: REDEFINITION must keep the inherited method interface. It cannot add this mandatory parameter.

options.text: Declare another format method with the same name and a different signature.
options.explanation: ABAP does not provide this ordinary same-name method overloading. A different signature needs a different supported design.

options.text: Change the inherited method to static only in the subclass.
options.explanation: A static method cannot replace the inherited instance method in this way. That does not solve the extra-input requirement.

options.text: Keep the inherited contract and add a distinct operation if needed.
options.explanation: The original operation remains usable by base-type callers. A separately named operation can explicitly require the new input.

prompt: Class A grants friendship to final class B. A has subclass A_CHILD. Which access follows automatically?

options.text: A can access B's private components.
options.explanation: The grant goes from A to B only. B would have to grant A access separately for the reverse direction.

options.text: B can access A's private components, but not A_CHILD's newly private components.
options.explanation: B receives access to A's private components. That does not automatically grant access to new private components declared by A_CHILD.

options.text: Every ordinary caller of B can access A's private components.
options.explanation: Calling B does not make the caller a friend of A. Friendship is not passed to ordinary callers.

options.text: A_CHILD must grant B the same friendship to preserve inheritance.
options.explanation: A_CHILD does not have to make B its friend. The grant made by A does not impose that new grant on its subclass.

prompt: References first and second point to the same object. CLEAR first is executed; second remains valid. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: The object is destroyed, so second becomes a dangling reference.
options.explanation: The second reference still reaches the object. Clearing first does not destroy an object that remains reachable this way.

options.text: The object's close method must execute automatically.
options.explanation: CLEAR does not call an application close method. Timely resource release needs an explicit owner and release path.

options.text: Only first is reset; the object is still accessible through second.
options.explanation: Only the first reference variable becomes initial. The second still points to the same object and can use it.

options.text: All instance attributes are reinitialized because one reference was cleared.
options.explanation: Clearing a reference variable does not reset the object's attributes. The second reference still sees the existing object state.

prompt: An approval service requires a repository but currently allows construction without one. Which change best establishes a usable object?

options.text: Require and validate the repository during controlled construction.
options.explanation: Creation can reject a missing or invalid repository immediately. A successfully created service is then ready for its documented operations.

options.text: Keep an initial repository and check only after the first posting.
options.explanation: This postpones detection until business work has already begun. Required setup should be checked before posting can happen.

options.text: Move the repository to public CLASS-DATA for callers to assign later.
options.explanation: Public class-level data lets callers change shared setup at any time. It makes valid construction and test isolation harder to guarantee.

options.text: Catch any later dereference failure and return approval success.
options.explanation: A missing repository is not successful approval. Catching the resulting error and reporting success hides the defect.

prompt: Test B passes alone but fails after test A changes a mutable class cache. B creates a new service instance. What is the most likely isolation problem?

options.text: An instance constructor cannot be called during ABAP Unit.
options.explanation: Tests may create ordinary objects. The issue is that class-level cache data survives the previous test.

options.text: Each NEW necessarily creates a second internal session.
options.explanation: NEW creates an object, not a fresh internal session. It does not isolate the existing class cache.

options.text: The class cache must be shared globally with all application servers.
options.explanation: CLASS-DATA is not automatically synchronized across application servers. Shared state within the relevant session is enough to cause this failure.

options.text: The new instance still sees class-level state left by the earlier test.
options.explanation: The new object still uses the same class-level attributes in that session. NEW does not reset the cache left by test A.

prompt: A price lookup returns an empty result for both missing price and database connection failure. What is the best correction?

options.text: Use CX_ROOT handling everywhere and retain the same empty result.
options.explanation: Catching more exceptions still leaves callers unable to tell missing data from a failed read. The outcomes need different meanings.

options.text: Distinguish absence from failure and preserve the technical cause when translating.
options.explanation: The caller can handle no price differently from could not read the price. Keeping the original exception also supports diagnosis.

options.text: Return price zero for connection failure to keep processing predictable.
options.explanation: Zero can be a valid price. Returning it for a connection failure can accidentally make an item free.

options.text: Expose the raw technical exception as the only contract for every client.
options.explanation: The service can provide a meaningful service-level error and keep the original cause. Every client does not have to depend on raw database exceptions.

prompt: A cart enforces positive quantities in add_item but exposes a writable reference to its actual item table. Which redesign best protects that invariant?

options.text: Keep the reference private but return it through a getter.
options.explanation: The getter still hands out writable access to the real table. Private attribute visibility does not prevent changes through that reference.

options.text: Rename the getter read_items and document callers as trusted.
options.explanation: Renaming the method does not remove the ability to insert a negative quantity. The rule can still be bypassed.

options.text: Return suitable value data and route mutations through validated cart operations.
options.explanation: A suitable value return avoids direct access to the internal table. Changes go through cart methods that check quantities; nested references still need care.

options.text: Copy only the reference into a new local variable before returning it.
options.explanation: The copied reference still points to the same table. A new reference variable does not create an independent table.

prompt: An existing provider cannot simulate prices. The common interface is being extended with simulate. What best avoids dishonest success?

options.text: Model simulation as an explicit optional capability with defined unsupported handling.
options.explanation: Clients that need simulation can request a provider that supports it. Unsupported providers can be reported clearly instead of pretending success.

options.text: Return an empty successful simulation from providers that cannot support it.
options.explanation: An empty success claims that simulation worked when it did not. The caller cannot make a reliable decision from that result.

options.text: Add simulate without checking any existing implementation.
options.explanation: Existing implementers are affected by the new method. Their implementation and activation must be checked before rollout.

options.text: Make callers catch every exception and interpret it as simulation success.
options.explanation: An exception may mean unsupported operation or a real failure. Treating either as success hides the result the caller needs.

prompt: A test intends to verify a discount threshold but replaces calculate_discount itself with a configured result. What should change?

options.text: Add more assertions against the configured result.
options.explanation: More checks of the same configured value still do not execute the real discount rule. A broken threshold could continue to pass.

options.text: Run the same mocked test in a different order.
options.explanation: Changing test order cannot restore the calculation that was replaced. The actual rule must run in its own test.

options.text: Mock the caller too so both sides agree on the expected value.
options.explanation: Replacing the caller too removes even more real behavior. Agreement between mocks does not prove the discount calculation.

options.text: Keep calculate_discount real and control its external dependencies.
options.explanation: The real calculation receives controlled inputs and produces the result. The test can then fail when the threshold rule is wrong.
